title: 冰袋、枕头和口令  (Ice, Pillows, and Orders)

segments.t: Ten minutes later in the café corner, Peng carries down two soft pillows for Mei's ankle while Qing hands Mei a clipboard and pencil. Listen first.
小美，脚后跟底下垫两个结实的枕头，严禁沾地。
好吧好吧——既然我不能站在炉子前，都给我仔细听好厨房规矩！
写字板准备好了，小美主厨！早上六点的面包面团归谁？
志鹏肩膀有劲——他来揉早上的面团，我看着计时器。
成交！以前我每个星期天都帮我奶奶揉大面包。
那谁来搅柠檬凝乳，谁来切扁豆汤里的胡萝卜呢？
小晴，你在我手边搅柠檬，志豪把每样蔬菜都切得精确到毫米！
相信我，志豪真会拿尺子量每一块胡萝卜丁的！
那我们给周经理安排什么活，既让他觉得帮上了忙，又不会打碎东西？
坐在桌子旁擦那十二只白瓷杯——离电灯开关和油漆远远的！
小美，现在把这杯洋甘菊茶喝了，上楼休息去吧。
六点整叫醒我——我不坐在那把椅子上，谁也不许碰我的烤箱！
Now let's go through it line by line with the English translation.
小美，脚后跟底下垫两个结实的枕头，严禁沾地。
'Two firm pillows under your heel, Mei, and strict orders not to touch the floor.' Peng jokes in mock-official style with the formal Chinese phrase meaning 'strictly forbidden to touch the ground'.
好吧好吧——既然我不能站在炉子前，都给我仔细听好厨房规矩！
'Fine, fine—if I cannot stand at the stove, listen carefully to my kitchen rules!' Slipping 'for me' right before the verb 'listen' in Mandarin adds classic head-chef authority: 'listen up for me!'
写字板准备好了，小美主厨！早上六点的面包面团归谁？
'Clipboard ready, Chef Mei! Who gets the six-o'clock bread dough?' Calling Mei 'main-kitchen'—the Mandarin noun for an executive chef—instantly wins her over.
志鹏肩膀有劲——他来揉早上的面团，我看着计时器。
'Peng has strong shoulders—he kneads the morning dough while I watch the timer.' Instead of a textbook word for 'strong', Mandarin says his shoulders 'have vigour', two punchy everyday syllables.
成交！以前我每个星期天都帮我奶奶揉大面包。
'Deal! I used to help my grandmother knead Sunday loaves every week.' Two syllables meaning 'complete the exchange' work just like snapping 'Deal!' in English.
那谁来搅柠檬凝乳，谁来切扁豆汤里的胡萝卜呢？
'And who whisks the lemon curd and chops carrots for the lentil soup?' Carrots are literally 'foreign radishes' in Chinese, named centuries ago when they arrived along the Silk Road.
小晴，你在我手边搅柠檬，志豪把每样蔬菜都切得精确到毫米！
'You whisk the lemons at my elbow, Qing, and Hao chops every vegetable to the millimetre!' Where English says 'at my elbow', Mandarin says 'at my hand-side' for working right within reach.
相信我，志豪真会拿尺子量每一块胡萝卜丁的！
'Believe me, Hao will measure every carrot cube with a ruler!' Peng teases his younger brother fondly—and in Chinese, diced food cubes use the tiny noun for a square peg.
那我们给周经理安排什么活，既让他觉得帮上了忙，又不会打碎东西？
'What job do we give Manager Zhou so he feels helpful without breaking anything?' Pairing 'both... and...' frames Qing's diplomatic balancing act for their eager boss.
坐在桌子旁擦那十二只白瓷杯——离电灯开关和油漆远远的！
'Polishing the twelve white cups at the table—far away from switches and paint!' An electrical switch is literally 'open-close' in Mandarin, naming the two things it does.
小美，现在把这杯洋甘菊茶喝了，上楼休息去吧。
'Now drink this chamomile tea and go rest upstairs, Mei.' 'Up-building' and 'down-building' are compact two-syllable action chunks in Mandarin—no separate word for 'stairs' needed.
六点整叫醒我——我不坐在那把椅子上，谁也不许碰我的烤箱！
'Wake me at six sharp—nobody touches my oven without me in that chair!' Adding 'whole' right after 'six o'clock' is how Mandarin says 'six sharp'.
Now let's listen to the whole conversation one last time.
小美，脚后跟底下垫两个结实的枕头，严禁沾地。

小美，现在把这杯洋甘菊茶喝了，上楼休息去吧。
六点整叫醒我——我不坐在那把椅子上，谁也不许碰我的烤箱！
With her foot propped high on pillows, Mei assigns every Wednesday morning kitchen station down to the last carrot! One scene left in Episode 4. See you next time.
明天见！
